overview: Our closest international getaway: a short flight to a country with tea hills, leopard safaris in Yala, scenic trains, elephants and calm south-coast beaches.
fit: Very good for both. Roads are slow, so keep the itinerary small.
season: December to April is best for the south and west coasts and hills. May–September is the southwest monsoon (rain on the west/south coasts). The east coast (Trincomalee) is best May–September.
gettingAround: Hire a car with driver for the trip (common and good value); scenic trains for one leg.

todo.title: Pinnawala or Udawalawe elephants
todo.why: Udawalawe safari to see wild herds

todo.title: Yala leopard safari
todo.book: Kids can join; dusty and bumpy

todo.title: Mirissa or Bentota beaches
todo.why: Calm beaches in season; whale watching Dec–Apr

todo.title: Galle Fort
todo.why: Walk the old Dutch fort walls

foodTips: Food is very familiar for us; vegetarian is easy.
save: Hire a car and driver for the full trip
Pay safaris and tickets in LKR, not USD
Skip the Ella–Kandy leg if time is short
safety: Road travel is slow; avoid night driving
Strong currents on some beaches; swim where locals do
kids: Elephants and the train are the 4-year-old's highlights

days.plan: Fly to Colombo; drive to Kandy
Nine Arch Bridge; drive to Yala

visa: Apply online for an ETA before travel. Sri Lanka has at times waived the ETA fee for Indians; check the official ETA site for the current rule.
